key_insight: Aberrant splenic arteries that arise from the SMA show geometry-driven flow disturbances—especially at the proximal segment—that appear to promote aneurysm formation and location.
clinical_relevance: This work suggests CTA-based morphologic and hemodynamic features could help identify patients with aberrant splenic artery anatomy who may warrant closer aneurysm surveillance.
method: Multicenter retrospective cohort of 195 patients with aberrant splenic artery anatomy from 16 Chinese centers.
3D CTA reconstruction measured 12 morphologic features and CFD estimated 14 hemodynamic parameters.
Selected 5 morphologic parameters to build a two-stage interpretable machine-learning model for aneurysm prediction and localization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports significant morphologic and flow differences between aneurysm and non-aneurysm groups, including lower proximal TAWSS, higher OSI at the junction, and a strong inverse correlation between OSI and branching angle.
watch_item: This is a retrospective model-development study, so external validation and prospective testing are still needed before clinical deployment.
paper_title: From Anatomy to Aneurysm: Morphological-Hemodynamic Coupling and Predictive Modeling in Aberrant Splenic Artery.
